articles.headline: 49ers rule veteran WR Mike Evans out after rib injury
articles.description: The 49ers lost veteran WR Mike Evans in the first half of Sunday's game against the Cardinals due to a rib injury.
articles.headlineJa: 49ers、肋骨負傷のベテランWRマイク・エバンスの離脱を発表
articles.descriptionJa: 49ersのベテランWRマイク・エバンスは、日曜日のカーディナルス戦前半に肋骨を負傷して途中離脱した。
articles.body:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- The injuries continue to mount for the San Francisco 49ers as receiver Mike Evans departed in the first half of Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals.

It was unclear exactly what happened to Evans, but he was slow to come off the field after a third-down pass from quarterback Brock Purdy intended for him over the middle fell incomplete. A few plays earlier, he got hit on the sternum during a completion over the middle but stayed in for a couple of snaps before departing.

Niners medical staff ran onto the field and helped Evans as he clutched at the right side of his sternum. Evans got up slowly and walked to the sideline where he entered the medical tent and, after a few minutes, got on a cart to go to the locker room.

At halftime, the Niners ruled out his return due to a rib injury. Evans, who managed a hip injury during the week, finished his day with three catches for 34 yards and a touchdown.

Cornerback Deommodore Lenoir, meanwhile, departed to be evaluated for concussion earlier in the half. He cleared that evaluation and returned to the game on Arizona's first possession of the third quarter.

articles.headline: Drake Maye: Patriots offense, own play 'unacceptable'
articles.description: Drake Maye, whose early-season struggles continued with two interceptions and a lost fumble in Sunday's 35-6 blowout loss to the Jaguars, called the offense's performance "unacceptable" as he looks within himself for answers.
articles.headlineJa: ドレイク・メイ、ペイトリオッツの攻撃と自身のプレーを「受け入れがたい」と批判
articles.descriptionJa: 日曜日のジャガーズ戦に35-6で大敗し、2インターセプトと1ファンブルロストでシーズン序盤の不振が続くドレイク・メイは、自らに答えを求めつつ、攻撃陣のパフォーマンスを「受け入れがたい」と語った。
articles.body:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- Patriots quarterback Drake Maye, whose early-season struggles continued with two interceptions and a lost fumble in Sunday's 35-6 blowout loss to the Jaguars, called the offense's performance "unacceptable" as he looks within himself for answers.

"It's disappointing. The ball starts rolling that way, we can't get out of our own way, and I can't get out of my own way personally -- I have to look myself in the mirror and take this as a turning point," he said.

"It's Week 3, and at the same time we have to have some fuel and realize that what we're doing out there offensively it's unacceptable. It's been unacceptable for three weeks. I have to start with myself, lead these guys, and get back after it."

Last year's MVP runner-up, Maye finished 14-of-25 passing for 199 yards, with no touchdowns and an 11.9 Total QBR, the lowest by a Patriots starter since Bailey Zappe (1.9) in Week 18 of the 2023 season against the New York Jets.

His six interceptions overall are the most by a Patriots quarterback through three games of a season since Drew Bledsoe had six in 1994.

"We haven't made good decisions with the football. We have to get it fixed," coach Mike Vrabel said after his team slipped to 1-2. "And everybody else has to do much better, starting with me."

In Sunday's loss, in which Maye was pressured on 11 dropbacks in the first half (his career high for a half, per ESPN Research), the turnover issues began late in the first quarter when the football slipped out of his hand while attempting a pass with the Jaguars recovering. Maye said after the game that center Jared Wilson had been bleeding on his hand, which led to the fumble on his pass attempt to receiver Kyle Williams.

"At the same time, I have to hold on to the football," he said.

Then, in position to slice into the Jaguars' 14-3 lead late in the second quarter, Maye threw an ill-advised pass on third-and-goal from the 2 looking for receiver Efton Chism III along the end line that cornerback Travis Hunter picked off for his first career interception.

"Just forcing it," Maye said of an issue that began in the fourth quarter of the season-opening loss to the Seahawks when he threw three fourth-quarter interceptions.

Maye also fired a third-quarter pick on a comeback route to Williams that he said he shouldn't have attempted.

After the game, Maye was asked if the right shoulder injury that led to him taking a pain-killing injection before Super Bowl LX in February has lingered at all early this season.

"I like to say that when you have that much time off and you get to focus on getting back, you're going out there healthy," said Maye, who previously noted the injury didn't require surgery.

"You're going to get banged up every now and then, but at the same time, a lot of guys are banged up. I'm looking forward to getting back to playing winning football, that's the main thing. And knowing I play a big role in that and taking the bull by its horns ... I wouldn't say

articles.headline: Vikings rule out Justin Jefferson with ankle injury
articles.description: Vikings star receiver Justin Jefferson was ruled out of Sunday's game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers after a first-quarter injury to his left ankle.
articles.headlineJa: バイキングス、足首負傷でジャスティン・ジェファーソンの途中離脱を発表
articles.descriptionJa: バイキングスのスターレシーバー、ジャスティン・ジェファーソンは、日曜日のタンパベイ・バッカニアーズ戦の第1クォーターで左足首を負傷し、途中離脱となった。
articles.body:
TAMPA, Fla. -- Minnesota Vikings star receiver Justin Jefferson was ruled out of Sunday's game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers after he suffered a first-quarter injury to his left ankle.

The injury appeared to occur on the Vikings' final offensive play of their first possession, at the end of a 10-yard catch on a screen play. Jefferson had caught a 22-yard pass earlier on the drive.

Jefferson never required medical assistance on the field but eventually had an extended visit in the blue medical tent. He emerged in the second quarter wearing his helmet and then watched the game from the sideline for a while, before he walked to the locker room. He was not seen on the sideline in the second half of the game.

In his absence, the Vikings shifted their offensive focus to No. 2 receiver Jordan Addison, who caught a 41-yard pass from Kyler Murray to give the team a 17-10 lead with 4:11 remaining in the second quarter. Jauan Jennings and Tai Felton were the Vikings' other receivers when they used three-receiver sets.

Jefferson has largely been healthy in his NFL career, playing in every Vikings game for five of his six full seasons. The lone exception was a torn right hamstring in 2023, an injury that cost him seven games before he was able to return.

He had the worst season of his career in 2025 as the Vikings tried to transition to quarterback J.J. McCarthy, while also using rookie Max Brosmer for two starts. He finished with 1,048 receiving yards for the season; that total in 17 games was less than he accumulated during his 10-game stint in 2023.

The Vikings' decision to replace McCarthy with Murray brought hope that Jefferson could resume his explosive production. He caught eight passes for 92 yards and two touchdowns in Week 1, mostly from backup Carson Wentz after Murray sustained a concussion, but managed only three catches for 55 yards in a rain-soaked Week 2 game at the Chicago Bears.

Jefferson's 179 receiving yards this season is the fewest he has had through three weeks in his career.

articles.headline: Several Panthers starters banged-up in loss to Browns
articles.description: The Panthers lost to the Browns 21-18 on Sunday, and they might have lost a few starters, at least temporarily, to injury in the defeat.
articles.headlineJa: パンサーズ、ブラウンズ戦の敗戦で複数の先発選手が負傷
articles.descriptionJa: パンサーズは日曜日に21-18でブラウンズに敗れ、この敗戦の中で、少なくとも一時的に複数の先発選手を負傷で欠く可能性がある。
articles.body:
CLEVELAND -- The Carolina Panthers lost to the Cleveland Browns 21-18 on Sunday, and they might have lost a few starters, at least temporarily, to injury in the defeat.

Quarterback Bryce Young (lower body), cornerbacks Jaycee Horn (quad) and Mike Jackson (groin), left guard Damien Lewis (elbow) and wide receiver Jalen Coker (quad) left the loss during various points due to injuries.

Young and Lewis, who were inspected by trainers, both returned to the field in the second half.

Following the game, Coach Dave Canales said Young was dealing with "something." When asked if the injury was related to Young's lower body, Canales affirmed the location.

"He's working through something, but he was able to finish," Canales said. "We'll give you more information on that once we get a full evaluation. But he was cleared to go back in and finish the game."

"There [were] a couple of balls that he would normally hit, so I'm wondering if he was working through something -- trying to find his base to get those balls off," Canales added. "He can make those throws, from different platforms and different things. He'd be the first one to tell you that up here. But he settled in, he found a way to play ball, and all of a sudden, we're moving the chains again and really just proud of how he battled us back right into the game."

Young, who threw for 291 yards, a touchdown and an interception against Cleveland, didn't make excuses for coming up short against the Browns. He also wouldn't provide detail on his ailment.

"Nothing -- it's football; we're all dealing with stuff," Young said. "It doesn't have any bearing on the game. Tough one, just didn't get it done."

Carolina was already without linebacker Devin Lloyd (calf), wide receiver Xavier Legette (knee) and safety Nick Scott (rib) against Cleveland. All three players were sidelined for the loss.

Coker, who battled an ankle injury leading up to the game, played throughout the first half but left with a new quad injury.

"His quad lit up on him a little bit," Canales said. "And so, the pain wasn't really going away. We're testing the strength, and we decided we couldn't put him back out there in that condition."

Jackson also left the game in the first half. Horn exited after the game-winning touchdown throw from Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson to tight end Harold Fannin Jr.

"We're going to have to evaluate that and see where he's at," Canales said about Horn. "But he was not going to be coming back in."

The Panthers will host the Detroit Lions (2-1) on "Sunday Night Football" in Week 4. They'll then have a bye in Week 5.

Longtime starting tackles Taylor Moton (blood clot) and Ickey Ekwonu (patellar tendon) are eligible to return from the non-football injury (NFI) list and physically unable to perform (PUP) list, respectively, following the bye. Defensive end Tershawn Wharton is also eligible to return from the PUP list after Week 4.

articles.headline: Travis Hunter happy to help Jags with first NFL interception
articles.description: Jaguars cornerback Travis Hunter finally grabbed his first career NFL interception Sunday.
articles.headlineJa: トラビス・ハンター、NFL初インターセプトでジャガーズに貢献でき歓喜
articles.descriptionJa: ジャガーズのコーナーバック、トラビス・ハンターが日曜日、NFLキャリア初となるインターセプトをついに記録した。
articles.body:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- It took 385 days, but Jacksonville Jaguars cornerback Travis Hunter finally grabbed his first career NFL interception.

And when he came down with the ball in the back of the end zone it came with a small dose of relief, too.

"Yeah, a little bit," Hunter said after the Jaguars' 35-6 victory over the New England Patriots at EverBank Stadium on Sunday. "Interceptions are great to catch, but I was focused on winning the game and continuing to focus on the next play."

Patriots quarterback Drake Maye was trying to hit receiver Efton Chism III in the back corner of the end zone on third-and-goal from the 2 with 1:02 remaining in the first half. Hunter outjumped Chism for the ball and the turnover preserved the Jaguars' 14-3 lead.

It was the first turnover Hunter has forced in his career. He had three pass breakups and 15 tackles in the first seven games of 2025 before a knee injury ended his season. He had one pass breakup and five tackles this season before Sunday.

"Travis to make the play, get the little bit of the monkey off his back a little bit in some ways to go out there and make a huge play [was critical]," Jaguars coach Liam Coen said.

Hunter came close to recovering Maye's fumble three plays earlier, but the QB recovered it at the Jaguars 5. That only added to his sense of urgency to finally grab his first turnover.

"I know he [Maye] tried me a couple times [with some throws], so I was just in there saying, 'I'm getting too close to the ball. I've got to get me one,'" Hunter said. "So we just continued to just do what the coaches schemed up for us and we just played our best part of it."

Hunter finished with four tackles on defense. He played five snaps on offense but didn't touch the football.

He has played 16 snaps on offense this season and has one catch and one carry, both of which came in the season opener against Cleveland.

articles.headline: Parma part ways with ex-Arsenal assistant Carlos Cuesta
articles.description: Parma parted ways with coach Carlos Cuesta on Sunday after winning only one of their opening five Serie A matches.
articles.headlineJa: パルマ、元アーセナル助監督のカルロス・クエスタ氏と契約解除
articles.descriptionJa: パルマはセリエA開幕5試合でわずか1勝にとどまり、日曜日にカルロス・クエスタ監督と解任・退任の道を歩むこととなった。
articles.body:
Parma parted ways with coach Carlos Cuesta on Sunday after winning only one of their opening five Serie A matches.

The club said Cuesta "has been relieved of his duty" and that "following an internal discussion between the club and coach, it was agreed that the conditions in order to continue this working relationship and the advancement of the sporting project, were not being met. Both parties came to a mutual agreement."

- Goals galore! Why Barça's start to season is best in Europe's top leagues for almost 100 years

- Udinese sign former Real Madrid defender Alaba

- Havertz back at Arsenal for injury treatment

A replacement was not immediately named.

Parma beat Genoa last weekend but only have four points.

Cuesta became the youngest manager in Europe's top five leagues, and the youngest Serie A manager in almost a century, when he was appointed by Parma in June 2025 at the age of 29. He had previously spent five years as assistant to Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta.

Having decided at a young age that his future lay in coaching rather than playing, Cuesta was given his first chance at Atlético Madrid with their underage teams and after four years there, went travelling Europe to study coaching methods.

It was during this period that Cuesta met Arteta, then part of Pep Guardiola's coaching staff at Manchester City, and after a two-year spell with Juventus' youth academy, Cuesta joined Arsenal in 2020.

He guided Parma to a 13th-place finish last season.

It's the third coaching change in Serie A this season after Paolo Vanoli replaced Fabio Grosso at Fiorentina and Raffaele Palladino replaced Domenico Tedesco at Bologna.

Parma's next match is at Serie A champions Inter Milan on Oct. 10 after the international break.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.headline: LaLiga chief Javier Tebas criticises Man City's alleged rule breaches: 'Equal rules for all'
articles.description: LaLiga president Javier Tebas has said Manchester City legal battle against the Premier League shows why "equal rules for all" are essential.
articles.headlineJa: ラ・リーガのテバス会長、マンCのルール違反疑惑を批判：「すべての人に平等なルールを」
articles.descriptionJa: ラ・リーガのハビエル・テバス会長は、マンチェスター・シティのプレミアリーグに対する法的闘争が、なぜ「すべての人に平等なルール」が不可欠であるかを示していると語った。
articles.body:
LaLiga president Javier Tebas has said Manchester City legal battle against the Premier League shows why "equal rules for all" are essential to protect football's integrity and sustainability.

ESPN reported on Friday that a source has confirmed City are expected to be found guilty on the vast majority of charges of financial breaches in their legal case with the Premier League.

In a statement, City didn't deny the guilty verdicts and said that the process "remains ongoing."

When contacted by ESPN on Friday, the Premier League said it wouldn't comment on a "private and confidential process."

The Athletic first reported Friday that City had been found guilty of all but one of the 115 charges by an independent panel.

- Ogden: Man City verdict will leave a stain and stench on a Premier League era

In 2020, Man City succeeded in overturning a two-year European competition ban from UEFA at the Court of Arbitration, after being found to have breached the governing body's Financial Fair Play (FFP) rule.

Tebas had previously spoken out against "so-called financial doping in European football".

In a lengthy post on X, Tebas reflected on those statements he had given during the Soccerex event, which had been held in Manchester during September 2017.

Tebas also called the CAS ruling a "deeply misguided decision" which was "extraordinarily damaging to the credibility of European football's economic control system" and again stressed the same rules must apply to all clubs.

"Economic sustainability is not bureaucracy. Financial control is not a whim," he said.

"And arguing that clubs should compete fundamentally with the resources they are able to generate doesn't mean being against any specific club either. It's about defending a model.

"A model in which sporting success doesn't depend on who has the most powerful financial backing behind them, but on who manages best, generates more resources, builds better teams, and respects the same rules as everyone else.

"Defending this position has cost me a lot of criticism and not a few headaches. But I still think exactly the same as I did in Manchester in 2017.

"There are principles worth defending, even if they come at a cost. And this one, for me, is one of them.

- Man City chairman on club's Premier League charges case: 'Nothing has changed'

"Now, almost nine years after those words at Soccerex, an independent Premier League commission has deemed 114 of the 115 financial breaches charged against Manchester City proven, according to the published reports.

"There's still a way to go. The sanction remains to be known, and the process isn't over. But what's happened once again shows why economic control, transparency, and equal rules for all are essential to protect the integrity and sustainability of football."

"We will keep defending those principles. Just like in 2017."

Information from PA contributed to this story.
